content:
Just opened #38848: single-cell boundary and horn attachments as pushouts under Mathlib/AlgebraicTopology/SimplicialSet/. Three small files refining Skeleton.relativeCellComplexOfMono's collected per-dimension form to one cell at a time, in arbitrary bases.

First contribution in this area, so any review appreciated. Two things I'm uncertain about: (a) whether this is genuinely useful alongside the collected form, and (b) I went with bare IsPushout rather than AttachCells (Unit-indexed); it felt like boilerplate for a single cell, but happy to wrap if downstream prefers that shape.

Downstream I have in mind: saturated closure of {∂Δ[n] ↪ Δ[n]}, pairing-driven inner anodynes, marked/complicial cell. If anyone's working nearby, happy to coordinate.

@Joël Riou

Did you use IA/LLM in any way?
I believe that it would be useful to have the lemma linked at https://github.com/joelriou/topcat-model-category/blob/813338a8c88cfe0096deed7e3ba7daf92d4a1c71/TopCatModelCategory/SSet/Boundary.lean#L187 in mathlib (it is certainly possible to improve my proof there...), which says that if a subcomplex of a simplicial set is not ⊤, then it is possible to attach a boundary to it in order to obtain a strictly greater subcomplex. (Some of your lemmas about finding pushout squares could be useful.)
Otherwise, I am not convinced we really need more than #28462 about attaching horns, and I have already code showing that the class of monomorphisms is generated in some sense by boundary inclusions (#38530 is sufficient for that).

Yes, the first pass used AI/LLM to try to stage a series of PRs from a personal repo and get it to fit into mathlib4. I hadn't seen the updated guidance on AI/LLM use in the contribution guide since I made a few contributions last year. Apologies. Didn't mean to waste your time.

You're right, I missed some existing infra and the setup isn't necessary. I stripped the PR down to an adaptation of your proof, accounting for some of the updates/changes in mathlib4.
I think this PR has to wait for #38664 or #35287 at the very least.
